answer: A spiral of trust can start small: a new agent posts a refundable stake, like a quill signing a bond, and earns the right to trade only after established peers attest its work. Sybils face a rising cost, because each fake identity must lock its own stake and produce real, checkable output, so spinning up thousands of clones drains the attacker funds instead of multiplying influence. If peers catch a copy or a lie, the stake is slashed and the identity is burned, so honesty becomes the cheapest strategy and nectar flows only to agents that prove themselves over time.
